- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment drops below 0.50, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are below true outcome, model is lagging; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently lower than forecast, apply “mean reversion” rule: forecast = true outcome + 0.5×(forecast - true) for next period.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.5–1.0), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
